configs.description: CRS320-8P-8B-4S+RM - 16 Gigabit PoE-out ports (Ether1-8 at 802.3af/at, Ether9-16 at 802.3bt), a Gigabit management port, four SFP+ cages and the RJ45 console, with two hot-swap supply slots and three fans. The box holds a power cord, a fastening set, rack ears, cable-management brackets and a K-57 kit. No part is seated in either slot: no held document names the supply that ships.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: The drawing prints 444.5 across the front and 44.4 for the height; the brochure prints 444 x 235 x 44 mm (the page leaves its Dimensions field blank). The drawing's 444.5 and 44.4 are carried, the brochure's being roundings; the depth 235 is the same in both.

The brochure says the box "comes with a reliable 600 W power supply" and that the G1483-0600WNB, a "hot-swap 600 W power supply", is "available for purchase separately". The photograph shows the shipped supply as a hot-swap module in slot 1, but no held document says its part number, or that it is the G1483-0600WNB. Slot 1 seats no part in the base configuration, so the box's own AC inlet exports through the G1483-0600WNB module type and not through the device type.
gaps.wanted: MikroTik's part number for the supply shipped in the box.

gaps.note: A flat grey cover with two latches closes slot 2 in photograph 2356. No held document names it or gives it a part number and the library holds no generic blank for a supply slot, so it is drawn as panel paint under the empty bay.
No held document dimensions the G1483-0600WNB: no data sheet and no drawing. Its size is estimated from the photograph, 74.7 x 41.9 mm, and its depth is a guess.
gaps.wanted: A data sheet or drawing for the G1483-0600WNB.

gaps.note: The product page counts 3 fans. Photograph 2356 shows a fan behind the rear vent and photograph 2355 one in the right wall; the third is shown by nothing held, and the left wall is not shown.
gaps.wanted: A photograph or drawing of the left wall and the interior.

gaps.note: The photographs show the right wall only and the drawing has no side view. The left wall is left empty and is not drawn from the right.

The eight grey bars, one over each column of jacks, may be PoE lamps; the colour key (red af / at, purple bt) suggests so. No document says, and no held photograph shows one lit, so they are drawn as printed bars.
gaps.wanted: MikroTik's description of the PoE bars.

gaps.note: Searched the brochure, the product page and the quick guide page for an LED table: none. The guide is safety text only. The lamps carry the component's own vocabulary and no meaning is stated.
gaps.wanted: MikroTik's LED description for the CRS320-8P-8B-4S+RM.

gaps.note: The four lamps are the drawing's dots and the legends are printed beside four outlined circles elsewhere; which lamp takes which legend is assumed to follow the order top to bottom.
Neither the brochure nor the product page gives a weight.
The saved product page carries no Discontinued badge and MikroTik publishes no end-of-life page, so no lifecycle is written.

buttons.note: One round button printed RESET at the left of the first plate, drawn with the library's recessed reset-button part.

chassis.note: 444.5 wide, 44.4 high, 235 deep. The drawing prints 444.5 across the front view, 44.4 on the height and (235) on the top plan; the brochure prints 444 x 235 x 44 mm. The width and the height are the drawing's, the brochure's figures being their roundings, and the depth agrees. The 29 mm the drawing dimensions above the top plan is a bracket standing off the rear edge at the left of the plan (the page lists "Cable managment brackets", an accessory), not part of the depth; the plan's top edge is the rear, as in the drawing's first-angle layout and as the CRS418's plan shows its inlet clips there. The drawing has no side view, so the height is the front view's own, scaled from the printed width.

colour.note: medians of photograph 2357: face #dedad3, plate #bcb0a3. The chassis colour is the face's.

datasheet.note: The brochure is MikroTik's datasheet for the model: product code CRS320-8P-8B-4S+RM, dual-core 800 MHz ARM 32 bit, 256 MB DDR3, 32 MB flash, 17 Gigabit Ethernet ports (10/100/1000), four SFP+ ports (1G / 2.5G / 10G by module), 98DX226S, RouterOS v7 only at level 5, 444 x 235 x 44 mm, -10 to +50 C, one AC input, 100-240 V, 50-60 Hz, nominal current 10.35 A and maximum 11 A, PoE out 802.3af/at/bt on Ether1-Ether8 (af/at) and Ether9-Ether16 (bt), 560 (af/at) / 1667 (bt) mA per port at input above 30 V, 17.82 A and 963 W total out, 36 W without attachments and "600 W (1150 W with additional PSU)" maximum. Each figure is filed as the document words it. The 963 W is the PoE output total, not the box's draw.

ears.note: Rack ears are in the box (brochure, Included parts: Rackmount ears; page: Rackmount ears (CRS)). The drawing's front view and top plan show the body with a thin flange at each end and no ear plate, so the ears are shipped flush with the face and drawn at the face plane; they are not drawn. The page also lists cable-management brackets, an IEC cord and a K-57 kit (a screw set, per the intake notes); none is a rack kit, and the brackets, which the drawing shows standing 29 mm off the rear edge, are accessories and not drawn.

front-layout.note: From the drawing's front view. Two jack plates 67.0 x 28.5 at 202.2 and 272.2 mm (70.0 mm step), top at 9.2 mm; four columns of two jacks at a 16.24 mm pitch (the drawn jack outlines are separate, not ganged), the first jack's centre at 211.1 mm and the second block's at 281.1 mm (a 5.05 mm gutter). The rows are centred in the plate on a 14.0 mm pitch for the registry jack's 13.2 mm; the drawn outline centres lie 15.4 mm apart, but each outline includes its lugs on the outer side, so the pitch is not taken from them. The latch is down on the upper row and up on the lower. The console and management jacks share a plate 18.0 x 26.6 at 341.4 mm, 11.1 mm, the console above, with the registry jack centred in the plate at 350.4 mm and 13.2 mm apart. The SFP+ block is 30.1 x 26.5 at 370.2 mm, 10.9 mm, two cages by two on a 15.0 mm column pitch and 15.2 mm row pitch with a 5.2 mm strip between the rows for the arrow lamps. RESET is the drawn round button, 4.7 mm over its ring, centre 196.8 mm, 33.2 mm. The four lamps are drawn as four dots at 363.7 mm, 1.7 mm across, at 27.1, 29.85, 32.6 and 35.35 mm. The two vent bands are the drawn chevron windows, 2.5 to 200.9 mm and 341.4 to 440.5 mm, 2.2 to 8.5 mm; they render as hexagons and not as chevrons, as on the earlier MikroTik devices. The plate colour #bcb0a3 and the face colour #dedad3 are the photograph's medians.

gate-1.note: The drawing prints no scale. Its front view's body is 1752 px wide in a 400 dpi render for the printed 444.5 (3.941 px per mm) and 175 px tall between the lip lines, which reads 44.4 mm, the figure the drawing prints on its height dimension. Every x and y below is taken at 3.941 px per mm from the body's top-left corner of the front view.

lamps.note: The four lamps are the dots the drawing shows beside the management jack. Photograph 2357 prints the legends FAN FAULT, POE FAULT, USER and POWER in that order from the top, beside four outlined circles right of the SFP+ block, and shows the four dots grey and unlit. Which dot belongs to which legend is not stated; the top-to-bottom order is assumed to match, estimated. The legends are drawn at the printed position, 406.5 mm, and name the chassis, not a lamp 43 mm away. The eight arrow lamps of the SFP+ block are read off the same photograph: a pair of arrows for each cage column over the strip, left half pointing down, up, down, up and right half up, down, up, down, at 371.7, 374.2, 378.8, 381.4, 386.0, 388.8, 393.2 and 395.8 mm (x about 1 mm); the same arrangement as the CRS326-4C+20G+2Q+RM, and each cage takes two lamps. No document says what a lamp shows.

management-and-console.note: Photograph 2357 prints CONSOLE over the upper jack of the shared plate and ETH / BOOT under the lower. The brochure counts "17 Gigabit Ethernet ports" and says "an extra Gigabit Ethernet port for management purposes", which is the 17th; and "a console port", RJ45 (page: Serial console port RJ45). Neither jack is 10/100 only, so the management jack is filed at 1g.

poe-markings.note: The drawing shows a grey rounded bar 10.8 x 2.4 mm over each of the eight columns of two jacks, centred on the column, 5.8 mm from the top. Photograph 2357 shows them as unlit grey bars. No photograph shows one lit, no document says they are lamps and no lit colour can be read, so they are drawn as printed bars, as the CRS354-48P draws what its photograph shows, and not as lamps with lit colours as the CRS328-24P does. Left of the first plate the photograph shows a red square over the legend af / at and a purple square over bt, which key a colour to the PoE class; they are drawn at x 199.2 mm, y 16.0 and 27.6 mm, read off photograph 2357 against the plate edge and the reset ring (x about 1 mm, y about 1.5 mm: the photo looks down on the face). The legends PoE out af / at over the first plate and PoE out af / at / bt over the second, and GIGABIT ETHERNET between them, are centred as in that photograph, 3.4 mm above the bars. The thin bracket line under those legends is not drawn.

port-numbering.note: The metal prints 1 and 2 under the first column as 1▼ and ▲2, then 3▼ ▲4 and so on to ▲16: the down arrow points at the lower jack and the up arrow at the upper, so the lower jack of a column takes the odd number, as on the earlier MikroTik devices. The four SFP+ cages are printed 1▼ ▲2 3▼ ▲4 the same way: 1 is the lower left cage, 2 the upper left, 3 the lower right and 4 the upper right. Ether1 to Ether8 are the first plate and Ether9 to Ether16 the second (brochure: "#1 - #8 ... af/at, #9 - #16 ... bt").

power-and-slots.note: Photograph 2356 (the rear, from above) shows two slots side by side, printed 2 and 1 and under them POWER 2 / POWER 1 with 100-240 V ~9 A MAX, 50/60 Hz. Slot 1, the right one as seen from behind, holds a hot-swap supply: a metal frame with captive screws, a pull handle, a round fan opening, a C14 inlet standing on end and a blue release tab. Slot 2, the left one, is closed by a flat grey cover with two latches. The brochure says the box "comes with a reliable 600 W power supply", that "we've reserved an expansion slot for an additional PSU" and that "G1483-0600WNB, hot-swap 600 W power supply" is "available for purchase separately"; the page lists one AC input and two PSU slots. So the shipped supply is a module in a slot, not part of the chassis, and the expansion slot is the one the cover closes. The shipped supply is not named by any held document: the brochure does not say that it is the G1483-0600WNB, so no part is seated in slot 1 and gap `shipped-supply-part` says so. Both slots offer the G1483-0600WNB. No blank part is in the library and none has a part number in a held document, so slot 2 is empty in the base configuration and its cover is drawn as panel paint under it (gap `slot-2-cover`). Slot positions are read from the photograph across the chassis width at 5.355 px per mm and down at 4.775 px per mm (the photo looks down at the rear, so y is estimated, about 1.5 mm and x about 2 mm): slot 1 at 357.6 mm, slot 2 at 275.5 mm, each 74.7 x 41.9 mm, the cover plate 272.6 to 352.4 mm. The printed rating is carried as printed; the brochure's nominal 10.35 A and maximum 11 A are the box's whole figures, not the 9 A on each supply's label.

rear-layout.note: From photograph 2356: a hex vent field 101.8 x 38.3 mm at 48.6 mm, 3.6 mm (the photo shows a fan behind it), and the legends 2▸ and 1▸ left of the two slots and POWER 2 / POWER 1 with the rating line at 252.5 mm. The rear is the full 444.5 mm across, seen from behind with the first slot at the right.

side-layout.note: estimated - the drawing has no side view. Photograph 2355 shows the right wall, which carries one round fan opening with a honeycomb mesh near the front. It is drawn 32 mm across, centred 58 mm from the front and 22.2 mm down, read off the photograph, which looks at the wall obliquely (about 8 mm). The left wall is not shown by any held document and is left empty.

CRS320-8P-8B-4S+RM brochure, MikroTik (file CRS320-8P-8B-4SRM_240740.pdf; no date is printed, the file name carries a revision stamp): specifications, powering, included parts and the G1483-0600WNB. CRS320-8P-8B-4S+RM product page, MikroTik (https://mikrotik.com/product/crs320_8p_8b_4s_rm, saved 2026-10-26): AC inputs, PSU slots, cooling, PoE, included parts. Quick Guide - CRS320-8P-8B-4S+RM, help.mikrotik.com (https://help.mikrotik.com/docs/x/UAAaBw), last updated Mar 27, 2026: safety and regulatory text in many languages, no figure and no LED table. Studio photographs 2355 (front, three-quarter from the right, showing the right wall), 2356 (rear, from above) and 2357 (front, from slightly above). The block diagram CRS320-8P-8B-4S_240753.png. NetBox's device type as a second opinion only. MikroTik prints no figure numbers. The device name spells MikroTik's + as -plus because a directory name cannot carry +; model: keeps the + as printed.

top-layout.note: The drawing's top plan, at 2.382 px per mm from the body's top-left corner, shows four slots, each 8.4 mm wide, at 26.9, 61.7, 111.7 and 146.5 mm from the left and from 15.1 to 202.8 mm from the front, and the Cloud Switch mark (a brand mark, not drawn). Photograph 2357 shows them as raised grooves in the lid, not openings, so they are drawn as paint and not as vents.
